paper_metadata.title: Atomic site location by channelling enhanced microanalysis (ALCHEMI) in gamma'-strengthened Ni- and Pt-base alloys

evidence.quote: Two ternary Ni–Al alloys with Cr and Ti additions were investigated.
For a ternary Pt–Al–Cr alloy, it was found that Cr atoms occupy Al sites.
For two ternary Ni 82Al12Ti6 and Ni 79Al15Cr6 alloys it was qualitatively found that Ti and Cr prefer the Al sublattice in the L1 2-ordered c0-phase.
For two ternary Ni 82Al12Ti6 and Ni 79Al15Cr6 alloys it was qualitatively found that Ti and Cr prefer the Al sublattice in the L1 2-ordered c0-phase.

The combination of ALCHEMI experiments and the calculated enthalpy of formation for c0-phases in the Pt 82Al12Cr6 and the Pt 77Al12Cr6Ni5 alloys showed that the addition of Ni is resulting in a reduction of the formation enthalpy and the lattice parameter and is therefore additionally stabilizing the L1 2-ordered structure.

mechanisms.name: tetragonal distortion of L12 lattice by Cr on Pt sites

evidence.quote: The calculated results demonstrate that Cr residing on Pt sites leads to a tetragonal distortion of the L1 2-ordered cell with a = 390.3 pm and c = 393.2 pm closely to the structure type Pb 3Sr with a = 383.2 pm and c = 389.4 pm observed by Stadelmaier et al. [39].

mechanisms.name: softening of lattice due to density-of-states peak at Fermi level

evidence.quote: A closer look to the Fermi level, Fig. 13 b, exhibits a local maximum of the total density of states for Pt 3Al and Pt 3Al with 3.125 at.% Cr atoms occupying the Pt sublattice at the Fermi level. This is an indication for a structural phase instability leading to a softening of the lattice which can be released by the onset of magnetism or a structural transformation [40].

mechanisms.name: L12 phase stabilization by Ni addition via reduced formation enthalpy

evidence.quote: The combination of ALCHEMI experiments and the calculated enthalpy of formation for c0-phases in the Pt 82Al12Cr6 and the Pt 77Al12Cr6Ni5 alloys showed that the addition of Ni is resulting in a reduction of the formation enthalpy and the lattice parameter and is therefore additionally stabilizing the L1 2-ordered structure.

This indicates that the enthalpy of formation is lower for Cr occupying the Pt sublattice but without retention of the L1 2-ordered structure, i.e. it does not contribute to a stabilization of the L1 2-ordered Pt 3Al phase.

conflicts.description: ALCHEMI experimental results show Cr preferring Al sites in Pt-Al-Cr, whereas first-principles calculations at 0 K show lower formation energy for Cr on Pt sites.

evidence.quote: The calculated formation energy for ternary Pt–Al–Cr alloys is lower for Cr occupying the Pt sites for both impurity concentrations. This is in contrary to the experimental ALCHEMI results.
